hero.title: Urethral stricture
hero.summary: Get care for weak urine flow, spraying, straining, repeated infection, retention, and urethral narrowing.

sidebar.ctaText: Book a consultation and review the cause.

body: A urethral stricture is narrowing of the urine passage. It can slow urine flow and make it hard to empty the bladder.
It may happen after injury, infection, catheter use, surgery, inflammation, or sometimes without a clear reason.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Common symptoms include weak urine flow, spraying, straining, long time to pass urine, incomplete emptying, dribbling, burning, repeated UTI, blood in urine, or sudden urine blockage.
Some people also feel lower abdominal discomfort due to poor emptying.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if urine flow is weak, symptoms are getting worse, infections repeat, or you have a history of catheter use, injury, or urethral procedure.
Seek urgent care if you cannot pass urine.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Tests may include uroflowmetry, post-void residual urine check, urine test, ultrasound, cystoscopy, retrograde urethrogram, and voiding cystourethrogram when needed.
The aim is to know the location, length, and severity of narrowing.

experience.title: Treatment options for urethral stricture
body: Treatment depends on stricture length, location, severity, previous procedures, and recurrence.
Short strictures may be treated with dilation or optical internal urethrotomy in selected cases. Longer or recurrent strictures may need urethroplasty.
experience.featureText: Care is planned around flow test, imaging, stricture length, recurrence risk, and long-term urine flow.

video.title: "A good stricture plan should focus on durable urine flow, not only temporary relief."

careGuide.title: Before, during, and after stricture care
careGuide.intro: Stricture care needs correct mapping and follow-up to watch urine flow over time.

tabs.label: Before Treatment
items: Share catheter, injury, or surgery history
Ask which test maps the stricture
Plan catheter care if surgery is advised

tabs.label: After Treatment
items: Report fever, pain, or blocked catheter

careGuide.note: Your plan will depend on stricture length, location, previous treatment, and test results.

items.question: Can urethral stricture come back?
items.answer: Yes. Recurrence risk depends on length, location, and treatment type.

items.question: Is dilation a permanent solution?
items.answer: Dilation may help selected short strictures, but recurrence can happen.

items.question: What is urethroplasty?
items.answer: Urethroplasty is reconstructive surgery to repair the narrowed urine passage.

items.question: Will I need a catheter?
items.answer: Many stricture procedures need a catheter for healing. Duration depends on the procedure.

items.question: When is urgent care needed?
items.answer: Urgent care is needed if you cannot pass urine or have fever with urinary blockage.
